decisions: | R-next | 2026-10-31 | Every command of the shared table (R459) names who may send it, and `Host::dispatch_as` checks that in Rust for every caller but the screen: `free` (anyone: reading, and organizing that is undone as easily, archive, pin, rename), `own` (an AI only in its own family, the conversations started from the same first one, and a new conversation; any other asks the person), `ask` (an AI asks the person; a person at a terminal may), `person` (only the person on the screen: signing in, answering a card, granting a folder, raising permissions, money, security settings, deleting for good, saving to a path) and `screen` (the screen's own plumbing, sent from nowhere else). `save_settings` that touches the permission mode, hooks, full trust, previews or start with the system is the person's alone. | Erick |

| R-next-2 | 2026-10-31 | Callers other than the screen read conversations through `conversations` and `conversation`, never `state` or `open`, so reading marks nothing seen. A conversation's state is said in plain words: `working`, `waiting` (for the person), `concluded` (its last reply ended with the agent's own closing box marked done), `ended` (ended without that), `interrupted` (Faber closed under it), `stopped`, `failed`, `new`; a list says `idle` for one not running and never reads conversation files. | AI (owner delegated) |
